scenes.title: The right conversation
scenes.viewerPurpose: Make the distinctive idea or tension understandable on first hearing. Introduce the book-specific proposal clearly and leave its fuller explanation for reading. Picture a useful account of needs and limits
scenes.composition: Two personal agents compare intentions before requesting a meeting
addOrChange: Replace abstract motif with two workspaces, private notes and one optional invitation.

cues.narration: Imagine an agent that finds people who want to work on the same problem as you.
cues.visualAction: An agent compares two project notes and finds a possible shared problem.

cues.narration: The Network of Intent proposes a network where personal agents compare needs before asking people to meet.
cues.visualAction: Show the agents exchanging relevant goals before a human meeting exists.

cues.narration: These agents would explain what you want now, what you can offer, and what must stay private.
cues.visualAction: Keep private notes closed while goals and constraints are selectively shared.

scenes.title: Private intentions
scenes.viewerPurpose: See two people whose availability may not match Imagine avoiding an unhelpful meeting Wonder what trust and privacy this would require
scenes.composition: A research request meets a potential partner’s full schedule
addOrChange: Add one project brief, availability calendar and optional meeting.

cues.narration: A researcher needs a collaborator; a potential partner has expertise but little available time.
cues.visualAction: Compare the needed expertise with the partner’s lack of time.

cues.narration: Finding that mismatch early could save both people another pointless meeting.
cues.visualAction: Withdraw the unsuitable meeting before either person must attend.

cues.narration: The book explores the trust, privacy, and business questions behind this possible network.
cues.visualAction: Keep evidence and disclosure choices beside the proposed exchange.

scenes.title: A network worth testing
scenes.viewerPurpose: Understand this is a proposal needing real tests Imagine a conversation that begins with being understood
scenes.composition: A small pilot tests the value of one proposed introduction
addOrChange: Add two independent decline controls and unanswered feedback fields.

cues.narration: The proposal still needs to prove that people would find those introductions useful.
cues.visualAction: Both people review the introduction without a fabricated success metric.

cues.narration: Could finding the right person begin with a conversation that actually understands what you need?
cues.visualAction: End with a possible conversation that either can still decline.
